summary: Usage Insights: missing route breakdown for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (all traffic grouped under "unknown")
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports that Usage Insights (Console > Usage/Cost > Route/Model breakdown) does not show route-level rows for their OpenAI-compatible usage. Instead, traffic appears either:
- not attributed to any route (missing rows for /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings), or
- grouped under a generic bucket like "unknown" / "unattributed" with correct totals but no breakdown.

Impact
- Customer cannot identify top cost drivers by endpoint for internal chargeback.
- Finance workflow blocked: export is not usable because route dimension is missing for their primary traffic.
- Customer is in active enterprise evaluation; this is a success criterion for beta.

Customer context
- AcmeAI is using Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenAI SDK pointed at Redwood base URL).
- They are comparing totals in Usage Insights vs billing export and invoice totals; totals match within tolerance, but route dimension is the blocker.

Environment
- Workspace: acmeai-prod
- Deployment mode: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Time range tested: last 7d and last 24h

Steps to reproduce (support)
1) In Console as admin, navigate to Usage/Cost > Route & Model.
2) Filter: Project=acmeai-prod, Time range=Last 7 days.
3) Observe: model rows appear, but route column is either blank/"unknown" or does not include /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings despite known usage.
4) Compare with request logs: requests are present and billed.

Expected
Route column shows canonical routes (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings) with per-route token in/out and cost.

Actual
Route missing or grouped; only model-level attribution is usable.

Initial triage notes
- Not a console rendering issue: API response includes route="unknown" for a large share of rows.
- Billing totals match; attribution dimension missing implies telemetry field(s) not being normalized/filled for OpenAI-compat path variants.

Investigation summary
- Reviewed raw metering/telemetry events for affected time buckets: route_template is empty for OpenAI-compat endpoints served via compat router.
- Route normalization library templates common Redwood API paths, but OpenAI-compat router uses alternate internal route names (e.g., /openai/v1/chat/completions or /v1/chat/completions with different handler tag) and did not pass the normalized route to the metering event emitter.
- As a result, the aggregation job buckets these as route="unknown".

Root cause
Route normalization mapping did not include OpenAI-compatible endpoints (and/or the compat gateway path did not call the shared normalization utility before emitting metering events). This caused missing/empty route_template on telemetry events, resulting in unknown route grouping in Usage Insights.

Customer-visible workaround (temporary)
- For now, customer can approximate by filtering on model + comparing request logs by path. This is not sufficient for finance exports.

Planned fix
- Update normalization mapping to include OpenAI-compatible endpoints and ensure compat router uses the shared templating utility when emitting metering events.
- Verify that both canonical route and route_group fields are set consistently (per ADR).
- No immediate historical backfill promised; customer expectation to be managed (see comms in comments).

resolution: Resolved via fix-forward: updated OpenAI-compat telemetry emission + route normalization mapping so metering events populate route_template/route_canonical for compat endpoints. New Usage Insights aggregations now show per-route breakdown for OpenAI-compatible traffic. Historical data during the affected period remains grouped under route="unknown"; no backfill committed for beta.
next_steps: Add documentation note (Usage Insights troubleshooting): OpenAI-compat endpoints may appear as unknown for historical windows; fix-forward behavior and how to validate.

Track as product/eng follow-up: consider targeted backfill option for enterprise evals once reconciliation tooling is in place (reference SUP-24811 for billing consistency concerns).
